subject: Co-term transition with surge buffer — renewal pricing options
messages:
From: Evan Roth <evan.roth@novacare.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@novacare.com
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Co-terming & surge buffer for renewal + growth

Marcus —

Quick note from procurement and our platform team: we expect a ~40% spike in inference usage over the next 90 days due to two upcoming feature launches. We're in renewal season and would like to:

- Add a short-term uplift that covers the spike (we prefer something that doesn't force an immediate annual commit)
- Co-term the account to 2027-06-30 so our billing and internal budgeting align with other vendor contracts
- Understand what discounts you can offer for a mid-contract top-up and whether Redwood supports a temporary "surge buffer" (pre-purchased credits we can draw down, ideally priced below on-demand rates)

I've attached a simple workbook with projected token counts and the PO team would like a ballpark to include on a formal PO. Can you and your team outline options (prorated top-up, short-term buffer credits, or an amendment to move to an annualized commit) and the pricing/discount math? We want to avoid a long procurement back-and-forth — a concise set of 2–3 options w/ invoice timing would help.

Thanks —
Evan

Evan Roth
Director of Platform Engineering, Novacare
E: evan.roth@novacare.com
T: +1 415-555-0189

Attachment: novacare_requested_uplift.xlsx (spreadsheet, 1 sheet)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Evan Roth <evan.roth@novacare.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Co-terming & surge buffer for renewal + growth

Evan — thanks for the context and the workbook, that was helpful. Quick read: you have a short, high-amplitude surge followed by a higher baseline. I sketched three pragmatic options below; attaching our pricing matrix so your procurement team can see the line items.

Option A — Pro-rated top-up (low friction)
- One-time top-up for the next 90 days priced at our standard committed rate, prorated to the remainder of your current term.
- No co-term; simpler for accounting, but you keep two amortization schedules.
- Typical turnaround: PO -> invoice within 3 business days.

Option B — Surge buffer (recommended for short spikes)
- Purchase buffer credits upfront at a discounted bulk rate (we propose 12% off on-demand for buffer purchase >= 500k tokens).
- Credits draw down over the next 6 months; any unused credits expire at the end of the buffer window OR can roll into a committed discount if you elect to annualize within 60 days.
- Can be invoiced as a one-line prepayment; co-term possible as an amendment.

Option C — Annualize & co-term (best unit economics)
- Move to a 12-month co-term ending 2027-06-30 and convert uplift into committed capacity.
- Graduated discount (8–15%) depending on total committed tokens; includes a small credit buffer for burst usage.
- Requires procurement/legal for amendment; typical lead time 10–14 days.

Questions for Novacare to narrow:
1) Do you want the buffer to be scoped as a prepaid credit pool (simplest) or as a temporary overage discount applied to excess usage?
2) Any internal constraint on contract/PO dates that forces co-term to be on the next invoice vs. a later amendment?

Ben — looping you for pricing tables and a sample amortization. Lauren — do you want to propose standard discount thresholds for a 12-month commit here?

Best,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0142

Attachment: redwood_pricing_matrix_v3.xlsx (pricing matrix, multiple tabs)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Evan Roth <evan.roth@novacare.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Oct 2026 15:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Co-terming & surge buffer for renewal + growth — pricing options (numbers)

Evan / Marcus —

Thanks for the workbook. I ran the numbers and laid out three numbered proposals so procurement can drop one straight into a PO. All pricing below is USD and excludes tax.

1) Pro-rated top-up (fastest)- One-time top-up: 600k tokens at committed rate $0.0012/token = $720
- Invoice on receipt of PO; no co-term; no long-term discount.

2) Surge buffer (preferred compromise)- Pre-purchase 1.2M buffer tokens at 12% off our standard on-demand ($0.0014/token on-demand -> $0.001232/token after 12% off) = $1,478.40
- Buffer valid for 180 days; unused credits may be converted into a committed credit with pro-rata discount if you lock to 12 months within 60 days (we'd convert remaining tokens into committed capacity and apply an additional 6% credit).
- We can invoice the buffer as a single prepayment (Net 30). Co-term included as an optional amendment.

3) Convert to 12-month co-term + uplift (best savings)- Commit to an additional 6M tokens over the remainder of the new 12 months; blended rate negotiable but starting point: 10% off published committed bands -> estimated effective rate $0.0010/token -> est. $6,000 uplift across the year with a 5% surge reserve included.
- Requires signed amendment; recommended if you expect sustained elevated usage.

Quick notes on mechanism: the buffer product is intentionally simple — prepay credits, draw down, and automatic notification at 80% drawdown with a recommended auto-topup trigger (opt-in). If you prefer a refund mechanism instead of conversion, we can do a partial refund of unused buffer credits at a 30% restocking fee.

Evan — if you want to move forward with the buffer, I'll prepare a one-line invoice and a short SOW amendment to document the window and conversion paths. Lauren — do you approve the 12% buffer discount as the standard for deals under $5k in prepayment?

Regards,
Ben Carter
Sr. Solutions Rep, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0194

Attachment: (pricing-comparison table included in redwood_pricing_matrix_v3.xlsx)

Subject: Re: Co-terming & surge buffer for renewal + growth — pricing options (numbers)

Ben / Marcus —

Thank you — option 2 (surge buffer) looks like the best fit for the short-term spike and keeps our procurement process straightforward. We'll take: 1.2M buffer tokens at 12% off, invoice Net 30.

Next steps from Novacare:
- I'll have procurement issue a PO using the attached template and reference deal NW-2026-Q4-0417.
- Please send a one-line invoice and a short amendment/SOW that documents the 180-day window, conversion option, and notification thresholds.
- Our legal team will expect a short amendment (2–3 clauses) — we can route to your legal once the SOW is attached.

If you can get the invoice and SOW today, procurement will try to cut the PO by Monday. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Cheers,
Evan
